en: Regarding the佚文 (佚文, *yìwén*—missing fragments) of the *Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment*:
Previously, I happened to obtain a single fascicle from the lower volume of the ancient Song edition of the *Mahāvaipulya Sūtra on the Realization of the Meaning of Perfect Enlightenment*.
It consists of one sheet with twenty lines, each line containing twelve characters. At the end of the sūtra, there is the notation: "Left Treasury Office, West Pan..."
Record of the printing by Li San-erlang of Langxiang (Line 1). Now, upon examining the text:

"You, virtuous son, shall attain the state of a practitioner in a future life. Do not allow evil Māras or various heterodox teachers to afflict your body and mind, causing you to fall into despondency.
Therein it says: "At that time, the World-Honored One... do not allow... [and so forth].
The one hundred and thirteen words beginning with "giving rise to despondency" (*sheng tuiqu*) are not found in any of the extant editions of the canon.

According to this scriptural text, in the *Yuánjué* (Perfect Enlightenment) assembly, twelve bodhisattvas each rose from their seats to pose questions on the Dharma, and the Buddha likewise answered each of them.
The scripture first provides a detailed account of these events in prose, and subsequently...
The verse repeats this; however, regarding the account of the final rising from one's seat and the dialogue between the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla and the Buddha, there is only prose and no verse.
Since the literary form is inconsistent, it is evident that this is a case of error or omission.
For those who now consult the old Tripitaka, I have recorded the full text here on the left.
December of the *xinhai* year of the Meiji era. Recorded by Matsubun.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
Worthy Bhadramukha, you should know that this sutra was spoken by all Buddhas; it is protected and upheld by the Tathāgatas.
It is the eye of the twelve divisions of the canon, titled the *Mahāvaipulya-bodhimaṇḍa-dhāraṇī-mantra* which reveals the realm of the Tathāgata.
Those who practice in reliance upon it will advance until they reach the stage of Buddhahood.

Just as the ocean receives the hundred rivers And those who drink from it are all filled, Even if one were to give seven treasures Heaped up to fill the three thousandfold world system, It would not equal hearing this sutra.
If one were to transform beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges So that they all attained arhatship, It would not equal hearing half a verse. You all, in future ages...
You are the protector who upholds this teaching; do not allow weariness or discouragement to arise.
